page: Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes two threads per core, 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16 support, alongside standard cryptographic and integer manipulation flags. System memory totals 64.0 GB, maintaining an even 4.0 GB allocation per vCPU. Local storage is provided by a bundled 320 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no discrete GPU accelerators included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance alongside robust memory throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests and PassMark memory evaluations, the instance registers in the top 10% of results. Geekbench single-core execution and large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth also place in the upper 25%. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics present a median profile: multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench compilation, image processing, and PassMark CPU tests reflect middle-tier execution typical of a 16-thread configuration bounded by a 2.0 GHz baseline clock rate.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers standard density suited for multi-tenant isolation through dedicated core allocations. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external input/output latency without introducing remote disk overhead. This balance of upper-tier single-thread speed, consistent dedicated compute, and local solid-state storage fits production workloads including relational databases, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD compilation tasks, and medium-scale web application serving.
description: Vultr voc-g-16c-64gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance configured with 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 8 physical AMD EPYC cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 320 GB NVMe solid-state drive. Operating at 2.0 GHz with multi-threading support and AVX-512 vector extensions, the instance provides 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU throughput and memory benchmark scores, coupled with strong large-block memory read and write bandwidth. Multi-core performance across compilation, encryption, and PassMark tests remains within the median tier, indicating predictable throughput limited by standard base clock speeds under full parallel load. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent execution free from multi-tenant CPU throttling. This balanced hardware profile functions efficiently for general-purpose enterprise application hosting, relational database operations, in-memory caching tiers, and backend web services requiring responsive single-thread performance and dedicated local NVMe storage.
